entries.name: PermissionKit
entries.note: Question construction, the ask queue and answers are in permission_question.rs, and the SDK re-exports them in permission_kit.rs. Not built: any channel that carries a question to a guardian, so apps cannot send one yet. Built 2026-10-17: the shell permission service (services/permission_kit.rs) takes an app question with ask, keeps it in one request center per shell thread, and returns the guardian answers with responses, scoped per app; the SDK sends it with permission_kit::ask. Built 2026-10-17: the guardian sheet (shell/guardian_sheet.rs) lists the oldest pending question as an alert card with one button per choice and answers it with respond; the shell's tick calls expire each frame so an unanswered question goes away on time, and the sheet closes with it (tests guardian_sheet::tests, services::permission_kit::tests). Not built: a live check on the lab machine, and no app can send a question on the lab image yet.
entries.ready_note: Main job built: apps ask through the permission service (services/permission_kit.rs, SDK permission_kit::ask), the guardian sheet answers the oldest question (guardian_sheet.rs), and unanswered questions expire in the shell tick. Not checked on the lab machine yet; the verify runner does that.

entries.name: PIP
entries.note: Picture-in-picture geometry is in pip.rs: the shrunken picture's size, the corner it rests in, and where a dragged picture snaps. Remaining: the shell must draw the picture above other windows, which this file does not do, and the wiring is not yet tested on the lab machine. Built 2026-10-17: shell/pip.rs draw_window fills the placed window above the windows and blits a frame already scaled to it, clipped to the surface (tests shell::pip::tests). Built 2026-10-17: Shell holds the window in shell/pip.rs Floating (controller, corner, aspect) and Shell::draw paints it over the screen between the menu bar and the dock while it is starting or active (Shell::pip_start, pip_stop; tests shell::pip::tests). Built 2026-10-17: the pip service (shell/services/picture_in_picture.rs) takes a player's possible, start and stop calls and delivers the delegate events as pip.will_start, pip.did_start, pip.will_stop and pip.did_stop (tests services::picture_in_picture::tests). Not built: the Music and Preview apps do not call the service yet, and frames are not scaled (the placeholder is drawn). Built 2026-10-17: the SDK client springboard/sdk/src/picture_in_picture.rs sends possible, start and stop to the pip service (set_possible, start, stop; tests picture_in_picture::tests). Still open: no player app calls the client yet.

entries.name: RunningBoard
entries.note: Focus, on-screen visibility and suspension of each app are modelled in the pure occlusion model, with a grace period before suspension. The model does not yet suspend processes or send memory-pressure events (task 008 is open), and there are no process assertions. Built 2026-10-17: memory pressure is parsed from /proc/pressure/memory and reported once per level change (core memory_pressure); suspend and resume map to SIGSTOP and SIGCONT (occlusion::signal_for). Built 2026-10-17: the shell feeds occlusion facts for each external app (background.rs Suspender: focus and whether a window is shown) and sends SIGSTOP after the grace period and SIGCONT on focus, only while the Suspend Background Apps switch (suspend_background, off by default) is on; turning it off resumes the stopped apps (tests shell::background::tests). Not built: covering is not known yet (a shown app is never stopped), audio playing in the background is not exempt, and apps are not told about memory pressure, which needs a protocol message. Built 2026-10-17: window covering is computed by is_covered (cuts the visible part of a window by each window above it; tests occlusion::tests); process assertions keep an app running (Event::Assertion). Still missing: the shell does not yet feed covering or assertions to the model, and memory-pressure events need a protocol message. Built 2026-10-17: covering is now fed by the shell (springboard/src/shell/mod.rs app_covered over the desktop stacking order, into background::Facts.covered); tests occlusion::tests and shell::background::tests::a_covered_app_is_stopped_after_the_grace_period. Still missing: apps cannot take process assertions over the protocol, and memory-pressure events are not sent to apps.
entries.ready_note: The main job, stopping and resuming apps by their run state (focus, shown, covered, after a grace period), is done: the pure model and the shell feed. Process assertions and memory-pressure messages to apps are open and need a protocol message.
